question: When you inherit stock from someone who died, what cost basis do you generally take for federal capital gains purposes?
true_option: A stepped-up basis — generally the fair market value on the date of death
false_option: A carryover basis — the price the deceased originally paid
true_claim_text: inherited assets generally take a stepped-up basis to date-of-death value
false_claim_text: heirs take the deceased person's original purchase price as basis
source: IRC § 1014 (IRS, Publication 551, Basis of Assets): the basis of property acquired from a decedent is generally its fair market value on the date of death; carryover basis applies to lifetime gifts under § 1015, not inheritances.
